items.q: The renal autoregulation range of mean arterial pressure is:
items.exp: Within auto regulation range (MAP: 80–180 mmHg); 40–240 is only the graph axis. (Book p738)

items.q: Which of the following statements about renal autoregulation is TRUE?
opts: Within the autoregulation range RBF and GFR are constant
Within the range RBF rises linearly with pressure
GFR falls to zero within the range
items.exp: Renal blood flow (RBF) and GFR are constant within the autoregulation range. (Book p738)

items.q: Match each autoregulation mechanism with its descriptor — 1) Myogenic reflex 2) Tubulo glomerular feedback … A) Adenosine mediated B) Stretch reflex
items.exp: Mechanisms: myogenic reflex (stretch reflex) and tubulo glomerular feedback (adenosine mediated). (Book p738)

items.q: Fill up: In response to a falling GFR (eg: pre-renal failure), the afferent arteriole undergoes ______, raising filtration.
items.exp: In response to ↓ GFR → afferent arteriolar vasodilatation → ↑ filtration. (Book p738)

items.q: Fill up: With ↑ GFR/tubular injury, more NaCl/KCl reaches the macula densa and releases ______, causing afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction.
items.exp: ↑ NaCl/KCl reach macula densa → adenosine → afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction → ↓ filtration. (Book p738)

items.q: In the glomerulo-tubular balance example at GFR = 200 ml/min, the amounts reabsorbed and excreted are:
items.exp: GFR 200: Na+ filtered 200 meq → 198 meq reabsorbed, 2 meq excreted (1%). (Book p738)

items.q: Which of the following statements about glomerulo-tubular balance is TRUE?
opts: The percentage of Na+ excreted remains constant as reabsorption compensates
The percentage of Na+ excreted doubles when GFR doubles
Reabsorption stays fixed while excretion rises
items.exp: ↑ GFR → ↑ reabsorption by tubule (compensation) → % of Na+ excreted remains constant (1% in both examples). (Book p738)
